verdicts.strongest_argument: The datum is real and I could not find it published anywhere — I re-ran the query and confirm zero entries for VENDOR_FULL_NAME 'C3.AI, INC.' signed 2026-08-01 to 2026-09-02, and zero under a loosened VENDOR_NAME:'C3' scan for 2026-07-01 onward, so it is not a name-variant artifact. But four things drain almost all the value out of it. (1) Reach: 1 Aug – 2 Sep 2026 sits in fiscal Q2 FY27, not in the quarter being reported (1 May – 31 Jul 2026). It can only touch tonight's print through forward commentary. (2) The hunter's in-quarter framing is selectively wrong. The reported quarter's three actions are not 'one of which was a deobligation' in any meaningful sense: they include a NEW $14,125,000 MDA Other Transaction Agreement (HQ0860269E011, C3 AI-DLA prototype) signed 2026-05-05 — the single largest new C3 obligation of FY2026 — against a $625k DOE descope. Net in-quarter FPDS flow is roughly +$13.5M, i.e. the opposite sign to the claim's tone. (3) Magnitude: the Aug-2025 comparison base is $4.38M of obligations, of which $4.231M is one lumpy Army action and the rest is $150.5k plus a $0 mod. Against FY27 revenue guidance of $210–240M that is under 2% of revenue in *obligations*, which recognise over years, and the comparison rests on n=2 prior Augusts. August is also not the federal year-end obligation month — September is — so the 'ahead of 30 Sept' premise is the wrong month. (4) A sector-wide explanation is already documented: the FY2026 continuing resolution barred DoD from new-start R&D and production-rate increases, and GAO found 36 of 74 DoD programs reporting CR-driven schedule delays in 2026. Separately, FPDS under-counts C3 structurally — C3 sells through Carahsoft's GSA MAS (47QSWA18D008F), where the FPDS vendor is Carahsoft, and through prime integrators such as ECS on the Army intelligence work, where the FPDS vendor is ECS. C3's total direct FPDS obligations for all of FY2026 are about $30.2M against ~$250M of revenue and management's stated ~45%-of-bookings federal/defense/aerospace mix, so the feed sees a minority of the federal business and its month-to-month variance is mostly noise. Finally the conclusion the datum points at — C3's federal execution is impaired — is already the consensus and already in the price: C3 AI Federal was reorganised inside the restructuring that took headcount from ~1,075 to ~700, an analyst asked directly on the 3 June call how that restructuring hit the $450M Air Force ramp, the stock is 46% off its 52-week high, D.A. Davidson carries Underperform at $7 into tonight, and the 25-delta skew is +18.98 vol points with the baseline reading 'downside paid'. New number, consensus inference, immaterial size, wrong quarter.

prior_publication.what_it_says: GAO documents that the FY2026 continuing resolution barred DoD new starts and production-rate increases, with 36 of 74 programs reporting CR-driven schedule delays — a sector-wide, already-known reason for a lull in new DoD obligations in 2026.

On the FQ4 FY26 call, management disclosed the restructuring that cut headcount from ~1,075 to ~700 and reorganised the federal division under new leadership, and was asked directly about the ramp of the $450M U.S. Air Force contract in light of that reorganisation.

D.A. Davidson reiterates Underperform with a $7 target into the FQ1 FY27 print, citing inability to underwrite durable subscription growth after a bookings miss — the bear case on execution is already the published sell-side stance.

C3 is listed among manufacturers resold under Carahsoft's GSA MAS contract 47QSWA18D008F, so agency purchases of C3 software book in FPDS under Carahsoft's vendor name, not C3.ai's — the feed's known under-report mode.
C3 works as a subcontractor to prime integrator ECS on U.S. Army intelligence modernisation, another route whose FPDS vendor of record is not C3.ai.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Skew_25d at +18.98 vol points with priced_direction_lean 'downside paid', 6 of 8 prior prints negative with a 25.6% max drawdown, spot 46.4% below the 52-week high, and a 12.7% event-implied move — the market is already paying handsomely for exactly this outcome. Working against me: run_up_5d is +7.71% and run_up_20d +4.93%, so the tape into the print is firm rather than sagging, which is why I am at 58 and not 75. There is no visible move on any date the FPDS gap became observable, because no one observed it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the August window fell inside the reported quarter, or if the missing obligations were sized in the tens of millions against direct-prime flow that FPDS demonstrably captures in full, I would drop this toward 20.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I pulled the same Greenhouse board and the counts broadly check out — 67 open roles, twelve federal/defense/intelligence-titled or Tysons-based, and yes, a second 'Executive Assistant to the CEO' in Tysons, Virginia. What does not check out is the novelty, and the per-posting dates are exactly the false-positive mode the brief flagged. The 'Senior Director, Product Management - C3 AI Defense and Intelligence' the claim calls 'newly created' was first published 2026-03-10 — nearly six months old, live before the reported quarter even began and before the 3 June print repriced the name. 'Senior Director, Strategic Solutions - Federal Defense Sector' was first published 2023-05-24, over three years ago; 'Data Scientist (Federal)' 2025-09-18; 'Senior Corporate Counsel - Federal' 2025-09-10; 'Senior/Lead SRE – Federal' 2025-10-03; 'Navy and Maritime Industrial Base' 2026-03-23. Only four of the twelve postdate the last print, and the requisition open since May 2023 is either evergreen boilerplate or a role nobody has managed to fill — both the opposite of a funding tell. The claim's direction is also contradicted by the company's own numbers: the 3 June call disclosed headcount going from ~1,075 in January 2026 to about 700 with ~$135M of annualised cost reduction, and third-party posting trackers show 75 C3 listings in August 2026 against the 67 live today, so the req count is shrinking. Sixty-seven openings at a company that just cut 375 people is backfill inside an announced restructuring, not expansion, and 'funded' is an inference a job board cannot support — FY27 guidance already embeds a $(128)–$(160)M non-GAAP operating loss, so this spend is inside guidance rather than incremental to it. Above all, the conclusion is the published bull case, not a discovery: federal/defense/aerospace bookings +89% y/y at ~45% of total bookings was disclosed and written up in February 2026, the $450M Air Force RSO ceiling and the $500M DoD OTA are company press releases, FedRAMP Moderate was covered in January 2026, and the Defense and Intelligence Suite has its own product page. The board itself is a public careers page mirrored on Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, LinkedIn and levels.fyi. This is agreement with the consensus long thesis dressed as a data pull.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Wire-level preview built entirely on the federal thesis: federal bookings +89% y/y at nearly 45% of total bookings, the ~$500M DoD contract, and FedRAMP Moderate authorisation.
Company press release raising the Air Force Rapid Sustainment Office award ceiling to $450 million — the funded defense vehicle the hiring would service, already announced.
Company press release on Army contested-logistics selection, part of the already-public defense build-out narrative.

C3's Tysons Corner office and its federal/defense openings (Army strategic solutions, federal contracting, defense product management) are indexed and publicly searchable on mainstream job aggregators.

Discloses the restructuring taking headcount from ~1,075 to ~700 with ~$135M of cost savings and the reorganisation of the federal division — the context that makes 67 open reqs backfill rather than growth.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: run_up_5d +7.71% and run_up_20d +4.93% into an amc print on a name 46% off its high: the tape has been bid for a week, which is what a market already leaning on the defense-pivot story looks like. Put/call open interest ratio of 0.05 on 135,726 contracts says the retail-facing side of this chain is overwhelmingly call-owned — upside optionality on exactly this thesis is what people already hold. The prior print on 2026-06-03 moved only -1.21%, so the defense narrative did not clear a bar then either.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the majority of the defense-titled reqs had first-published dates after 2026-06-03 and the total req count were rising rather than falling from 75 to 67, I would move this to around 35.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Three of the four legs of this composite were published by the company itself, two of them in dedicated press releases, and the fourth has no mechanical path to a revenue print. Snabe's leave of absence — and therefore his not standing — was announced in a C3 press release on 2026-06-22, filed as an 8-K on 2026-06-24 (items 5.02/7.01/9.01), picked up by TradingView and StockTitan and analysed by Simply Wall St; the proxy's 'not standing' language is the mechanical consequence of a leave the company itself publicised, so the hunter's 'eleven weeks after C3 celebrated Snabe's appointment' irony is a juxtaposition of two facts C3 volunteered. Dwyer's appointment and the exact $900,000 initial option award vesting over five years are in the 8-K filed 2026-08-25 and were written up in a Yahoo/Simply Wall St piece on 2026-08-31, which explicitly judged the appointment 'incremental rather than a major shift' next to the consumption-pricing transition. The new General Counsel's 826,901 RSUs effective 2026-07-30 were the subject of a Businesswire press release on 2026-08-04 and covered by StockTitan and others — that is wire copy, naming Tom MacMitchell and the vesting schedule. What is genuinely un-picked-up is Rice: I searched repeatedly and found no press coverage of her not standing for re-election, only the DEF 14A itself filed 2026-08-27 with no accompanying 8-K. So there is one obscure-but-public leg here, and I would score that leg alone around 35. Against that, the mechanism does not reach tonight's print at all: a Class III director retiring at 70 after seventeen years on a board that is being deliberately shrunk from twelve seats to eleven is a governance datum, not a revenue, bookings or guidance datum, and nothing about it lands inside the quarter ended 31 July 2026. The reading that a Cooley litigation partner and former Acting Associate Attorney General plus a new GC equals legal battening-down is inference layered on published facts, and the tape has been up 7.7% over the five sessions spanning both the proxy and the 8-31 write-up — the market saw this and bought.

prior_publication.what_it_says: C3 press release announcing Snabe's EU Special Envoy appointment and stating he will take a leave of absence from his C3 roles for the duration — the company disclosed the board departure itself, ten weeks before the proxy.
8-K coverage of Snabe stepping back from the C3.ai board for the EU envoy role.
Item 5.02 8-K appointing John C. Dwyer a Class III director, disclosing the initial option award with a $900,000 grant-date fair value vesting over five years.
Published analysis of the Dwyer appointment two days before the print, concluding it is incremental and that the consumption-pricing shift matters far more than one added independent director.
Press-release coverage of the 826,901-RSU inducement grant to new SVP and General Counsel Tom MacMitchell, effective 2026-07-30, with the full vesting schedule.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: run_up_5d of +7.71% brackets the 2026-08-27/28 proxy filing and the 2026-08-31 Dwyer write-up: the stock rose through both. No adverse repricing is visible on the dates these facts entered the record, and there is no governance-specific footprint in the option surface — the +18.98 skew is the standard pre-print downside bid on a name that has fallen 18.5% and 25.6% on prior reports.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If Rice's exit were accompanied by an 8-K disclosing a disagreement, or if the proxy tied the board turnover to a specific federal contracting or securities-law exposure, the Rice leg would carry real weight and I would drop the composite to about 30.

interactions: AI-1#0 and AI-1#1 are direct mirror images resting on the same question — whether C3's federal/defense business is stalling or accelerating — measured through two different live feeds that return opposite answers. Both cannot be edge. A scorer that takes both at face value nets them toward zero while double-counting the research effort, and if either is right it argues the other's proxy is unreliable: if the Greenhouse defense build-out is real and funded, the FPDS August blank is a measurement artifact, and if the FPDS blank is a real demand break, the Tysons reqs are unfunded aspiration. My dates favour the artifact reading of #0 (CR new-start freeze, reseller/prime routing) and the stale reading of #1 (most reqs predate the 3 June print). Second interaction: AI-1#1 and AI-1#2 both hinge on the same unstated 'C3 is deepening its Washington footprint' inference — #1 reads the Tysons Executive Assistant posting as commitment while #2 reads the loss of Rice, the company's most prominent Washington name, as retreat. They cannot both be the signal, and neither is sourced to a company statement of intent. Third: AI-1#2's Snabe leg and the 8-K record behind it come from the same self-disclosure stream (press release 2026-06-22, 8-K 2026-06-24) that also carries the June restructuring detail I used against AI-1#1, so #1 and #2 are partly grounded in one corpus C3 published voluntarily. Finally, the same FPDS extract underpins both halves of AI-1#0, and reading it in full inverts the in-quarter conclusion: the hunter's chosen quarter contains a new $14.125M MDA Other Transaction Agreement signed 2026-05-05 that the finding does not mention.
